title.en: At least 13 killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza after Hamas agree disarmament deal
title.zh: 哈马斯同意解除武装协议后，以色列对加沙发动袭击，造成至少13人死亡

summary.en: Israeli strikes on Gaza City, Khan Younis, and Deir el-Balah resulted in at least 13 deaths. Israel stated its targets were military operatives, and these strikes occurred after Hamas had agreed to a disarmament deal.
summary.zh: 以色列对加沙城、汗尤尼斯和代尔巴拉赫的袭击造成至少13人死亡。以色列表示，袭击目标是军事人员，这些袭击发生在哈马斯同意解除武装协议之后。

body.en:
At least 13 people, including several children, have been killed in the latest strikes on Gaza, Palestinian officials have said.

Gaza's Civil Defence Authority said Israeli military aircraft carried out the attacks on Gaza City, Khan Younis and Deir el-Balah.

It was the second successive night of Israeli strikes on the territory, and it comes days after Hamas accepted a disarmament plan, which would see the Palestinian group hand over its weapons to US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace.

A spokesperson for the Israel Defense Forces (IDF), said it was targeting military operatives in Gaza, and two Hamas militants were killed.

The Israeli Energy Minister, Eli Cohen, said on Sunday that no deal had been reached to stop attacks on the Gaza Strip, a territory now under 70% Israeli control.

Cohen added that he saw a need for the strip to be placed under the full control of Israel if Hamas did not disarm - despite the Board of Peace plan for Israel to pull out of the territory - the Reuters news agency reported.

In a post on X on Sunday, the IDF said it had killed two Hamas commanders, one from the elite Nukbha force, and one from the Maghazi Battalion.

The IDF also said killed another Hamas militant from the Jabalia Battalion in northern Gaza in a separate attack last week. It said all three were planning to attack Israeli targets.

Palestinian health officials said two people, including a child, were killed in a strike on a residential building in Gaza City, while another person was killed near Jabalia in northern Gaza.

A father, mother and their nine-year-old son were killed after a strike on a house in Khan Younis, and a man and woman died after their apartment block was struck in Deir el-Balah.

More than 1,100 Palestinians have been killed since a supposed ceasefire came into effect last October.

Last week, President Trump said the Board of Peace had reached an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza.

On Friday Trump insisted that Israel was "very happy" with the proposed agreement, describing it as a "big step for the Middle East".

But Israel remains deeply sceptical about Hamas' willingness to give up its weapons or its control in Gaza. Far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir dismissed the draft as "not acceptable".

It is part of the second phase of a US-brokered Gaza ceasefire plan that aims to end the war in Gaza.

The 20-point plan, unveiled in September last year, included the creation of the Board of Peace to oversee the agreement's implementation, as well as the disarmament of Hamas, withdrawal of Israeli troops and reconstruction of Gaza.

A 15-point road map was also published on Friday, which sets out the final steps for implementing the agreement.

title.en: Ukraine says major Russian oil refinery and airfield hit, as Moscow reports eight deaths
title.zh: 乌克兰称袭击了俄罗斯主要炼油厂和机场，莫斯科报告八人死亡

summary.en: Russia's military reported attacking Ukraine's ports and vessels in the Black Sea overnight, following Ukraine's claims of hitting a major Russian oil refinery and airfield. Moscow also reported eight deaths.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯军方称，在乌克兰声称袭击了俄罗斯一主要炼油厂和机场后，俄军连夜袭击了乌克兰在黑海的港口和船只。莫斯科还报告了八人死亡。

body.en:
Ukraine has said it carried out overnight strikes deep inside Russia, hitting a major oil refinery and an airfield that houses Russian strategic aviation.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the Engels airfield and the refinery, both in the Saratov region some 600km (373miles) from Ukraine's border, were hit. An oil depot was also struck in Kaluga region and a drone launch site in Bryansk.

Russia said eight people were killed in the Ukrainian strikes, and 635 drones shot down or intercepted. It also reported yet another strike on a warehouse of Russia's biggest online retailer Wildberries.

Meanwhile, Moscow said its forces attacked overnight two Ukrainian ports and two vessels in the Black Sea.

Later on Sunday, Ukraine said one person was killed in a Russian strike on a postal terminal near the north-eastern city of Kharkiv.

Both Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified attacks focusing on major cities, energy facilities and warehouses, as the vast front line remains virtually static and US-led mediation attempts to end the war have shown no breakthrough.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In Sunday's post on social media, President Zelensky described the latest Ukrainian strikes as "our long-range sanctions" against Russian facilities that he says finance Moscow's war.

He said the Engels airfield and Saratov oil refinery were "strategic facilities".

The Ukrainian military said in a separate statement that its attack triggered a blaze at the airfield - one of the main bases of Russia's strategic aviation.

It said Tu-95MC and Tu-160 bombers were regularly using Engels to launch missile strikes against Ukraine.

Saratov regional Governor Roman Busargin admitted that "a drone attack caused damage to civilian infrastructure in Saratov and Engels". He later said that two people were killed.

Separately, three people were reported killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on a civilian vehicle in Russia's Udmurtia region, and another three in the Belgorod region bordering Ukraine.

In the Samara region, Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev described a strike on a Wildberries warehouse that caused a fire as "yet another terrorist act" by Ukraine.

In recent weeks, Ukraine has hit a number of Wildberries logistics hubs, describing them as legitimate targets providing the Russian military with drone components, navigation equipment and other gear.

Ukraine's attacks are reported to have had a serious impact on the Russian economy, especially on hundreds of small and mid-sized businesses using the retailer.

Meanwhile, Russia has been recently targeting warehouses of Ukraine's Nova Poshta postal company and major online retailers like Rozetka.

title.en: Helicopters fighting Greece wildfires collide in mid-air
title.zh: 扑灭希腊山火的直升机在空中相撞

summary.en: Video of the incident shows one of the helicopters hitting the propellers of the other, which bursts into flames.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two helicopters have collided in Greece as they were battling to control wildfires.

Video of the incident some 65 km (42 miles) west of the capital, Athens, shows one of the helicopters hitting the propellers of the other, which bursts into flames. Both fell into a ravine. Two of the four crew members involved were found unconscious, Greek media report, with the others sustaining light injuries.

Several fires have broken out in Greece this week, prompting many people to leave their homes. Strong winds have hampered efforts to bring the blazes under control.

Several other European nations have suffered devastating wildfires after a succession of heatwaves created favourable conditions for them.

Early this week, France and Spain battled huge fires - two of the main ones were close to Madrid and Bordeaux respectively. Those have now been contained, though they are still burning. Some 300,000 people who were evacuated have started to return to their homes.

In Greece, media reports describe "a titanic battle" along a swathe of territory that includes Porto Germeno, Psatha, Fokida, Megara and Kefalonia, where more than 500 firefighters have been struggling to bring the situation under control over the past 72 hours.

The mid-air collision occurred "during a forest firefighting operation in the Psatha area," the Fire Department announced.

The crew members - two Greek and two Romanian, according to Greek media - have been taken to the 251st Air Force General Hospital.

Most wildfires are sparked by people, whether intentionally or accidentally, but climate change is making the conditions for them more common.

Last winter was mild and wet, encouraging vegetation growth, which has then dried out in successive hot spells, generating fuel for wildfires.
body.zh: 希腊两架直升机在奋力控制山火时相撞。 事件发生在首都雅典以西约 65 公里（42 英里）处，视频显示其中一架直升机撞上了另一架直升机的螺旋桨，后者起火。两人都掉进了山沟里。据希腊媒体报道，四名涉事船员中的两人被发现昏迷不醒，其他人受轻伤。 希腊本周发生多起火灾，迫使许多人离开家园。强风阻碍了控制火势的努力。 在连续的热浪为它们创造了有利条件后，其他几个欧洲国家也遭受了毁灭性的野火。 本周早些时候，法国和西班牙发生了大火，其中两场主要火灾分别位于马德里和波尔多附近。尽管它们仍在燃烧，但现已得到控制。约30万撤离人员已开始返回家园。 在希腊，媒体报道描述了包括Porto Germeno、Psatha、Fokida、Megara和Kefalonia在内的大片领土上发生的“一场巨大的战斗”，过去72小时内，500多名消防员一直在努力控制局势。 消防部门宣布，这起空中相撞事故发生在“普萨塔地区森林消防行动期间”。 据希腊媒体报道，机组人员——两名希腊人和两名罗马尼亚人——已被送往第 251 空军总医院。 大多数野火都是由人为引发的，无论是有意还是无意，但气候变化使野火的发生变得更加普遍。 去年冬天气候温和湿润，促进了植被生长，但随后植被在连续的炎热天气中变干，为野火提供了燃料。

title.en: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
title.zh: 小昆虫，大危害：全球蚂蚁贸易蓬勃发展

summary.en: Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?

They are unusual pieces of evidence that regularly appear in Kenyan  courtrooms: thousands of ants packed into tiny containers.

Since 2025, such finds have been presented in court several times. Staff from the Kenya Wildlife Service discovered them during baggage inspections. In multiple cases, they identified thousands of specimens of the sought-after Messor Cephalotes species also known as the Giant African Harvester Ant . A single queen can fetch more than €200 ($230) on the market.

The export of wild animals is generally prohibited in Kenya. Due to high levels of poaching — particularly involving elephants and rhinoceroses — many African countries have introduced tough laws against wildlife trafficking.

Kenya has also tightened its legislation. Under these rules, a Chinese  national who attempted to export ants was sentenced last April to one year in prison for biopiracy. Given the growing scale of smuggling and its ecological consequences , the judge said the sentence should serve as a deterrent.

It was already the second major ant-smuggling case in 12 months. The previous year, the wildlife service stopped four men who referred to themselves as the "Ant Gang." Among them were two 19-year-old Belgians  who were trying to smuggle 5,500 queens to Europe. They were fined around €5,000 each.

Whenever such cases arise, authorities often call entomologist Dino Martins to the airport. "I was shocked," he said. "Not only by the sheer number of ants, but also because they were queen ants."

The seized insects were young queens that had been dug up from nests in the ground, according to Martins, who has led several research institutes in Kenya and is regarded as one of Africa's leading ant experts, These queens have wings that allow them to fly away and establish new colonies.

"When you collect queens at this critical moment, you interrupt a key stage in the creation of new colonies," he said, adding that Kenya's ecosystems are also affected because ants transport grass seeds, helping to regenerate the savannah.

In Europe, keeping ants as pets has become increasingly popular, particularly among young people. Colonies are housed in glass terrariums where a queen produces offspring and establishes an entirely new population.

One person who keeps ants as a hobby is Michael Meier, who asked not to be identified by his real name. While at university, he wanted a pet that required little attention.

"With ants, it doesn't really matter whether I feed them today or tomorrow," he said.

At one point, Meier kept almost 30 colonies in a...
body.zh: 无论合法与否，运往欧洲的非洲蚂蚁贸易正在蓬勃发展。爱好者们对这些昆虫有何吸引力？这种贸易对生态系统造成了哪些风险，包括停电？ 它们是肯尼亚法庭上经常出现的不寻常证据：数千只蚂蚁被装在小容器里。 自 2025 年以来，此类调查结果已多次提交法庭。肯尼亚野生动物管理局的工作人员在行李检查时发现了它们。在多个案例中，他们鉴定了数千个备受追捧的 Messor Cephalotes 物种（也称为巨型非洲收割蚁）的标本。单个蜂王在市场上的售价可以超过 200 欧元（230 美元）。 肯尼亚普遍禁止出口野生动物。由于偷猎现象严重（特别是涉及大象和犀牛），许多非洲国家都出台了严厉的法律来打击野生动物贩运。 肯尼亚还加强了立法。根据这些规定，去年四月，一名试图出口蚂蚁的中国公民因生物剽窃被判处一年监禁。鉴于走私规模不断扩大及其对生态造成的影响，法官表示，该判决应起到威慑作用。 这已是12个月内第二起重大蚂蚁走私案。去年，野生动物服务部门拦住了四名自称“蚂蚁帮”的男子。其中有两名 19 岁的比利时人，他们试图将 5,500 名王后走私到欧洲。他们每人被罚款约 5,000 欧元。 每当出现此类情况时，当局通常会叫昆虫学家迪诺·马丁斯到机场。 “我很震惊，”他说。 “不仅因为蚂蚁的数量庞大，还因为它们是蚁后。” 马丁斯表示，被查获的昆虫是从地下巢穴中挖出来的年轻蚁后。马丁斯曾领导过肯尼亚多家研究机构，被认为是非洲领先的蚂蚁专家之一。这些蚁后拥有翅膀，可以让它们飞走并建立新的蚁群。 他说：“当你在这个关键时刻收集蚁后时，你就中断了新蚁群创建的关键阶段。”他补充说，肯尼亚的生态系统也会受到影响，因为蚂蚁会运输草籽，帮助大草原的再生。 在欧洲，饲养蚂蚁作为宠物越来越受欢迎，尤其是在年轻人中。蜂群被安置在玻璃容器中，蜂王在那里产下后代并建立一个全新的种群。 迈克尔·梅尔 (Michael Meier) 是一位以养蚂蚁为爱好的人，他要求不透露自己的真实姓名。在大学期间，他想要一只不需要太多照顾的宠物。 “对于蚂蚁来说，我今天或明天喂它们并不重要，”他说。 迈尔曾一度在一个……中饲养了近 30 个菌落。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to stewardship, provision, and the common good. 1 Peter 4:10 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with stewardship that serves neighbours, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到管家责任、供应与公共福祉。1 Peter 4:10提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以服事邻舍的好管家心态来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: Moscow restaurant blast a 'brutal terror attack,' mayor says
title.zh: 莫斯科市长称餐厅爆炸为“残酷恐怖袭击”

summary.en: An explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square, described by Mayor Sergei Sobyanin as a "brutal terror attack," resulted in fatalities. The mayor vowed that those responsible would be punished, though many questions about the incident remain unanswered.
summary.zh: 莫斯科市长谢尔盖·索比亚宁称，库德林斯卡亚广场一家高档餐厅外发生的致命爆炸是“残酷的恐怖袭击”，并承诺将惩罚肇事者。然而，关于此事件的许多问题仍未解决。

body.en:
The deadly explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square was a "brutal terror attack," Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, promising the perpetrators would be punished. But many questions remain.

An explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow killed at least three people, including the suspected bomber on Saturday night, authorities said.

"Law enforcement agencies are investigating the circumstances of the incident. Those responsible for this crime will certainly be found and face the punishment they deserve," he said in an online post on Sunday.

Russia's Anti-Terrorism Committee said a woman carrying  "a homemade explosive device" tried to enter the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square but was stopped by a security guard.

The device exploded at the entrance, killing the woman, the guard and a restaurant patron.

State news agency RIA Novosti reported that at least 21 other people were injured in the blast, which occurred shortly before 8 p.m. local time (5 p.m. UTC).

The restaurant's website said the venue had been closed on Saturday for a private event.

Heavily armed law enforcement officers sealed off the area and launched an investigation.

Authorities did not immediately identify those they believed to be behind the attack.

Russia has faced several attacks since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022. They blamed a ‌series of assassinations and attempted killings on Kyiv. Russian officials have yet to comment on any possible Ukrainian involvement into the Kudrinskaya Square blast.

However, Ukraine used drones to attack other parts of Russia on Saturday evening and early on Sunday, including a bombing which targeted an apartment block and killed two in the city Engels, some 900 kilometers (560 miles) southeast of Moscow.

Russia's Defense Ministry also said Kyiv struck a warehouse belonging to Wildberries, a major online retailer in Russia, with the Ukrainian drones hitting a site in the Samara Oblast, deep inside Russian territory. Regional Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said it was not immediately clear if there were any casualties.

Russian officials also reported over a 100 Ukrainian strikes in the Belgorod Oblast, which borders Ukraine. They said Kyiv forces used artillery, rocket launchers, and drones, leaving 14 people injured.

Over 200 Ukrainian drones have allegedly been shot down during the wave of attacks.

Meanwhile, at least one person was killed and seven wounded in the Russian attack on Ukraine's Kherson, with the attack involving artillery fire.

In Dnipro, seven passengers were wounded in a drone strike on a minibus, with the regional military administrator Oleksandr Hanzha describing it as a "deliberate and cynical attack on civilians."

reflection.en: In the wake of such a brutal act, the natural human response can be to seek retribution in kind. Yet, Yahweh's word calls us to a different path, reminding us not to be overcome by evil, but to actively overcome evil with good. This challenges us to seek justice and peace in ways that break cycles of violence rather than perpetuate them.
reflection.zh: 在如此残酷的行径之后，人类自然的反应可能是以牙还牙。然而，雅伟的话语呼召我们走一条不同的道路，提醒我们不要被恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。这挑战我们以打破而非延续暴力循环的方式寻求公义与和平。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

title.en: Five dead, 41 missing in Indonesia ferry fire
title.zh: 印度尼西亚渡轮火灾致五人死亡，41人失踪

summary.en: Five people have died and 41 are missing after a passenger ferry caught fire off the coast of South Sulawesi, Indonesia, marking the country's second ferry accident in two months.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚南苏拉威西省望加锡市附近发生一起客运渡轮火灾，造成五人死亡，41人失踪，这是该国两个月内发生的第二起渡轮事故。

body.en:
Five people have been killed and 41 are ‌still missing after a ‌ferry caught fire off Indonesia's Madura island, the country's search and rescue agency says .

⁠The Mutiara Santos 2 was carrying 271 passengers and crew members, with 225 people rescued, said the regional Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency on Sunday evening. A search ⁠and ‌rescue operation is ongoing.

The ferry ‌was heading from Surabaya in East Java province to Makassar city in South Sulawesi.

It was unclear how it caught ‌fire. Madura island is located off the northeastern coast of Java. Java and Madura are next to Bali.

Basarnas, Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency also said some passengers jumped into the sea and were picked up by a nearby ship. Four other vessels were on standby near the ferry but could not approach because of the risk posed by flammable material on the ferry.

The captain had called the ferry company to report the fire but had not been in contact since, Basarnas added.

A larger rescue operation was heading to the site from Surabaya, a six-hour journey from the site of the disaster, Basarnas said.

"Based on preliminary reports from the field, passengers are waiting to be evacuated by the vessels in the vicinity of the incident site," Muhammad Masyhud, a senior official at the Ministry of Transportation, said in a statement.

"The safety of passengers and crew is our top priority. We are continuously coordinating with all relevant parties to ensure that the evacuation process can proceed quickly, safely, and effectively."

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia , an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, partly due to lax safety standards and unpredictable weather.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank last month while sailing near Selayar, a small tropical island south of the much larger Sulawesi. At least four people were found dead, and 14 others remained missing until the end of the search operation.

title.en: Poland: Prime Minister Tusk defies anti-Ukrainian violence
title.zh: 波兰总理图斯克谴责反乌克兰暴力

summary.en: Anti-Ukrainian sentiment is increasing in Poland, leading to attacks against refugees from the war in Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has publicly condemned this violence and issued a warning about the threat from Russia.
summary.zh: 波兰国内的反乌克兰情绪日益高涨，针对来自乌克兰战区的难民的袭击事件频发。总理唐纳德·图斯克公开谴责了这种暴力行为，并就俄罗斯的威胁发出了警告。

body.en:
Anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland is on the rise, with numerous attacks against refugees from the war in Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has spoken out against the violence and warned of the danger from Russia.

The Polish leader didn't mince his words. "We must wage a resolute fight against this violence, because thugs, hooligans, and this culture of violence are becoming increasingly brazen and insolent — and also because they have received political support," Donald Tusk said on Tuesday, before a Polish cabinet meeting in Warsaw. The liberal-conservative prime minister said he deplored the fact that "more and more such incidents" are taking place all over Poland .

Tusk's comments came in response to an incident in Wroclaw two days earlier, in which three Polish men brutally beat up a young Ukrainian man and his girlfriend on the street. Cellphone videos show the attackers kicking the Ukrainian man as he lies on the ground. The woman was also hit, sustaining injuries to her neck and ear.

The attack came after an argument in a shop; the attackers took exception to the couple's Ukrainian accents. Polish police acted swiftly: Two of the attackers, both of whom have previous convictions, are already in custody, and a third is being sought.

Tusk warned that such incidents negatively impact Poland's image abroad. The country's reputation was greatly enhanced by its willingness to provide assistance after the start of Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine . This could be destroyed, said Tusk, "if we allow thugs, hooligans and common criminals to beat and humiliate people just because they have a slightly different accent."

Poland provided military and humanitarian assistance to its neighbor from the very beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. It took in more than one million refugees from the war, and around 1.5 million Ukrainians are currently living in Poland. The majority of them work, pay taxes, and contribute to the Polish economy.

But four and a half years after the start of the war, the mood in Poland has changed. More and more often, Ukrainians are being verbally and physically attacked in public. Last Wednesday a Polish manager on a construction site in Skawina, near Krakow, was filmed aggressively insulting Ukrainian workers. In another incident on a local train near Warsaw, two drunken men shouted verbal abuse at a Ukrainian passenger. On July 11, a man on a bus in Bielsko-Biala insulted and threatened two Ukrainian girls who were trying to take a selfie. Even schoolchildren, including teenagers at a playground, have fallen victim to the new climate of hate.

title.en: Trump holds off new Iran attack, in hope of a swift deal
title.zh: 特朗普将暂缓对伊朗发动新袭击，寄望迅速达成协议

summary.en: US President Donald Trump announced he would delay a new attack on Iran, expressing hope that negotiators could quickly reach an agreement to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，他将推迟对伊朗的新一轮袭击，并希望谈判人员能迅速达成协议，以“立即、全面、彻底”地重新开放霍尔木兹海峡。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump will hold off a fresh attack on Iran as long as a deal can be reached quickly to halt Iran's nuclear ambitions and re-open the Strait of Hormuz.

According to a post by Trump on his Truth Social platform, Iran and "other Middle Eastern countries" have asked for a time to complete a deal that would lead to "the Immediate, Complete and Total" reopening of the Strait and "an end to Iran's nuclear threa t.

"Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL," he said on the post.

Eli Cohen, Israel's energy minister and a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s security cabinet, said there was close security and intelligence coordination between Israel and the US on everything happening in the region.

But he added: "With or without an agreement, and regardless of any external commitments, if Iran attempts to renew its nuclear programme or advance its ballistic missile industries, we will be there. We will take action, and we will strike."

Trump and Netanyahu met in Washington on Tuesday, with an Israeli official saying they had explored all possible paths to curb Iran's nuclear program, including diplomacy, economic pressure and force. Iran denies seeking a nuclear weapon.

Trump's apparent de-escalation after days of threats of new attacks from each side was the latest twist in the war the US and Israel launched five months ago. Attacks have spread across the Gulf to the Red Sea and even a Mediterranean facility in Egypt.

Iran has warned the US this weekend against any "adventurous action" and said it would retaliate decisively if US forces followed through on Trump's threats of fresh attacks on Iranian targets.

Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi's made these comments in separate phone calls with senior Turkish, Pakistani and Saudi officials hours after Kuwait's army said it destroyed hostile drones launched by Iran against several vital facilities.

In his discussion with Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Araghchi said Iran would respond decisively to any "aggression" and discussed the consequences of “destabilising actions" by the US, as well as prospects for heightened regional insecurity. This was published on Araghchi's Telegram account.

body.zh: 只要能够迅速达成协议以制止伊朗的核野心并重新开放霍尔木兹海峡，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普就将推迟对伊朗发动新的攻击。 根据特朗普在其真相社交平台上发布的帖子，伊朗和“其他中东国家”已要求一段时间来完成一项协议，以“立即、全面和彻底”重新开放海峡并“结束伊朗的核威胁”。 他在帖子中表示：“基于这一请求，我同意，为了世界未来的利益，也为了一个成功和繁荣的伊朗的生存，取消这次袭击，但前提是能够迅速达成协议。” 特朗普还表示“以色列与我一起做出这一承诺”，尽管以色列尚未就这一评论发表公开声明。 伊朗本周末警告美国不要采取任何“冒险行动”，并表示，如果美军兑现特朗普的威胁，对伊朗目标发动新的袭击，伊朗将采取果断报复。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 在科威特军队表示摧毁了伊朗针对多个重要设施发射的敌对无人机几小时后，伊朗外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇在分别与土耳其、巴基斯坦和沙特高级官员的电话中发表了上述言论。 阿拉格奇在与巴基斯坦陆军参谋长阿西姆·穆尼尔元帅和土耳其外交部长哈坎·菲丹的讨论中表示，伊朗将对任何“侵略”做出果断反应，并讨论了美国“破坏稳定行动”的后果，以及地区不安全加剧的前景。这是在 Araghchi 的 Telegram 帐户上发布的。 阿拉格奇后来告诉沙特外交大臣费萨尔·本·法尔汉亲王，美国和以色列的任何袭击或地区国家参与此类行动都将得到“适当的回应”。一名美国官员告诉 Axios，沙特王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼周六与特朗普通话，“表达了担忧并要求澄清”美国对伊朗的计划。 隶属于伊朗最高安全机构的媒体《Nournews》表示，美国对伊朗能源基础设施的袭击将促使伊朗对沙特阿拉伯和阿联酋的油田以及卡塔尔和以色列的天然气田发动袭击，并称“所有这些都将被烧成灰烬”。 周五在戴维营休养所举行的内阁会议上，特朗普表示，他相信美国谈判代表，包括他的女婿贾里德·库什纳、特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和国务卿马可·卢比奥，仍然可以与伊朗达成协议。 但特朗普也表示，他对伊朗人失去了信心，他说，“他们经常食言”——德黑兰经常这样说……

title.en: China: Dozens dead in Gansu flash floods
title.zh: 中国：甘肃山洪致数十人死亡

summary.en: Chinese authorities will launch an investigation into the floods, amid warnings of further landslides as the rainy weather continues, after dozens were killed in Gansu province.
summary.zh: 中国当局将对甘肃省的洪水展开调查，同时警告称，随着降雨天气的持续，可能还会发生更多山体滑坡，此前甘肃省已有数十人死亡。

body.en:
Chinese authorities will launch an investigation into the floods, amid warnings of further landslides as the rainy weather continues.

The death toll after a flash flood in the northern Gansu province of  China has climbed to 25, according to state media reports.

The flood has left 23 others injured, the ⁠official Xinhua news agency reported on Sunday.

The Shuangshimen Scenic Area, a popular tourist spot for camping, was hit by a flash flood on July 26, with state media initially reporting 10 deaths and 23 injuries.

The country's national commission for disaster prevention said it would oversee an investigation into the event.

Videos of the flood show a deluge ripping through a valley where several tents and cars were parked.

Authorities have warned of further landslides, including in ‌Dingxi, ​as heavy downpour continues in the annual flood season.

Beijing and Inner Mongolia also issued weather warnings on Sunday as China's ​weather observatory warned of heavy rain, high winds and thunderstorms across a large stretch of the country from ⁠the southwest ​to the northeast.

title.en: UK court allows plans for Chinese 'super' embassy to advance
title.zh: 英国法院批准中国“超级”大使馆建设计划

summary.en: A UK court has dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which is set to become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, had cited security concerns regarding the embassy's presence.
summary.zh: 英国一家法院驳回了针对中国驻伦敦新大使馆的法律挑战，该大使馆建成后将成为英国最大的使馆。此案由一个社区协会提起，理由是该大使馆构成安全威胁。

body.en:
A court dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which could become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, argued the embassy poses a security threat.

A UK High Court on Friday threw out a challenge against UK authorities' decision to permit a new Chinese super embassy in central London .

The challenge was brought by a neighborhood group called the Royal Mint Court Residents' Association (RMCRA), which represents families and businesses in roughly 100 properties around the planned embassy site.

The RMCRA argued the presence of the embassy could increase the risk of terrorist attacks, lead to the targeting of dissidents and be used to enforce "draconian" Chinese laws in the UK.

The association also claimed that the embassy could pose a fire risk, arguing that Chinese authorities might ignore safety obligations that would be difficult to enforce because of diplomatic immunity on the embassy site.

On that basis, the group argued the development should not have been approved by the UK government as well as the London Borough of Tower Hamlets.

Yet in its ruling on Friday, the High Court said the "RMCRA ​did not produce reasonable ⁠and convincing evidence of the likelihood that a violation of human rights ⁠affecting them ​personally would occur."

In a move that was widely seen as a goodwill gesture toward Beijing, the embassy received approval from the UK government shortly before then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited China in January this year. 

 If completed, the new Chinese embassy would be the largest embassy in the UK .

Beijing plans to build the embassy on the site of the former Royal Mint, next to the Tower of London. The site covers around 20,000 square meters (235,000 square feet).

Beijing purchased the property in 2018 for a reported $327 million (€283.9 million), with the intent of relocating its embassy there from its current premises in Portland Place.

In response to the verdict, the RMCRA said it would seek permission to appeal, hoping to take the case to the UK Supreme Court.

"Beijing thinks this judgment is the final word. It isn't. The appeal is already in the works," Luke Pollard, head of the RMCRA, said in a statement.

Activists from  Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement living in exile have also been skeptical of the project, telling DW they fear the embassy could help Beijing suppress dissidents abroad. 

The UK is home to the world's largest Hong Kong diaspora, with an estimated 285,000 people of Hong Kong origin living in the country.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

title.en: 'That was crazy': Australia's historic Commonwealth Games day ends with a bizarre twist

summary.en: A midnight medal ceremony and a scaled-back format made for an unconventional Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Australian athletics team had its biggest one-day medal haul at the Commonwealth Games on Saturday, ending with a peculiar medal ceremony in a near-empty stadium.

Hours after the Games' athletics program ended, the Aussie men's sprinters were still waiting for their victory to be confirmed after protests over the other podium placings.

When the 4x100 relay team collected their medals in a makeshift ceremony along with the Canadian silver and Nigerian bronze medallists, the clock was ticking towards midnight.

The crowds at Glasgow's Scotstoun Stadium were long gone, with less than a hundred people remaining — mostly made up of Games officials, team staff, journalists and volunteers.

It was an odd ceremony for a major championship, with Australian winner Josh Azzopardi admitting with a smile: "That was crazy! We'd been waiting around not really knowing what was going to happen. It's definitely unique."

"We won gold, felt like it was ages ago now," said his teammate Lachlan Kennedy.

The holdup was the result of Canada's protests over their initial disqualification for a supposed illegal changeover, which was first upheld and then deliberated upon by the jury at great length until Canada was cleared for the silver.

It was an unusual conclusion to Australia's most successful athletics day ever at the Games, with a record haul of seven gold medals and 17 medals in total, including two events where the Aussies swept the podium.

Australia's previous record was set more than 70 years ago, with six gold medals and 11 medals in total in 1950.

It capped off the penultimate day of a stripped-back Games that had been quirky from the outset .

Victoria was originally supposed to host , but withdrew in 2023 due to rising costs. At the time, it prompted some to question the relevance of the Games and whether the event had a future at all.

The following year, organisers announced that Glasgow would step in as host city, with its Games to be supported in part by money from Victoria. The Victorian government had to pay a compensation of $589m including a $380 million settlement to cancel its hosting obligations.

While the Games has always had fewer sports and athletes than the Olympics, the 2026 event was even more pared back.

The 2022 Birmingham Games featured 20 sports and more than 5,000 athletes, while Glasgow hosted just 3,000 athletes competing in ten sports.

Some onlookers said the vibes in the city were vastly different to 2014, when it last hosted the Games.

title.en: 'At least there was closure': NT Police reflect on the discovery of Kumanjayi Little Baby
title.zh: “至少有了了结”：北领地警方回顾Kumanjayi Little Baby的发现

summary.en: Police in the Northern Territory reflected on the five-day search for Kumanjayi Little Baby, highlighting the intensive efforts of officers and the significant community support that led to the discovery and provided closure.
summary.zh: 北领地警方回顾了对Kumanjayi Little Baby为期五天的搜寻工作，强调了警员们的不懈努力和社区的大力支持，最终找到了失踪者并带来了了结。

body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the name and image of an Indigenous person who has passed away.

They didn’t seek the spotlight, but these Northern Territory Police officers found themselves in it.

Sergeant Chris Harden and acting sergeant Karl von Minden were among the investigators who found the body of five-year-old little girl Kumanjayi Little Baby on the outskirts of Alice Springs.

The little girl’s name has been changed for Warlpiri cultural reasons; under Indigenous protocol, it is taboo to speak the name of someone who has died.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The two officers spoke exclusively to SBS News for the first time about the enormous five-day search effort that made international headlines.

It culminated in the discovery of her remains, and within hours the arrest of 49-year-old Jefferson Lewis, who has been charged with her murder.

The two search and rescue specialists were having an extremely busy year. The top end of Australia is flood and cyclone central, and they’d been travelling from disaster to disaster.

Von Minden’s job was to coordinate and oversee the sprawling search operation that involved a call out for volunteers; hundreds arrived, some even flew to Alice Springs to help.

Harden was on the front lines of the grid search, walking metre by metre through buffel grass that had grown high and ominous in the summer rains, wrangling a group of volunteers each day.

"There was holes, washouts, everything which you just could not see," Harden recalled.

"There was a big risk that someone was get bitten by a snake, fall down a hole, do an ankle. But everyone was united. The community were just unbelievable."

Both of them barely slept and neither of them had worked on a search of that scale and complexity before.

"That was quite a unique operation, I think, across the territory. We have coordinated quite large search and rescues before, but never to the scale where we had so many civilian volunteers helping and the amount of people out there and the terrain that we were looking at," von Minden said.

"You go outside and suddenly there's 200 people volunteering, putting their name down, wanting to search," Harden said.

Their police colleagues, the SES, Defence, fire services and all the government agencies and organisations that downed tools on their normal jobs to join forces in the quest to locate the little girl.

"If we didn't have that, yeah, we could still be, you know, searching for her," Harden said.

title.en: 'We committed 7 years ago': SA forges ahead with Indigenous truth-telling commission
title.zh: 南澳州推进原住民真相委员会，称“七年前已承诺”

summary.en: South Australia is proceeding with its Indigenous truth-telling commission, fulfilling a seven-year-old commitment despite the national Voice referendum's failure in 2023.
summary.zh: 尽管2023年全国原住民之声公投失败，南澳大利亚州仍将履行七年前的承诺，继续推进其原住民真相委员会。

body.en:
South Australia will stand up a truth-telling commission over coming months, extending a Voice-to-treaty framework that cements the state as the second-most advanced jurisdiction on the Uluru Statement's unfinished agenda.

Speaking to NITV's John-Paul Janke and Natalie Ahmat on the broadcaster's Garma set, against a backdrop of stringybarks rising from the red Arnhem Land dirt, Acting Premier Kyam Maher said the state government would spend $8.5 million on a commission that will run a truth-telling process and advise on a possible treaty.

The commission is the next stage in a program South Australian Labor has pursued since 2019. Responding to the Uluru Statement from the Heart — the 2017 declaration by Indigenous leaders calling for a Voice to Parliament, treaty and truth-telling — was among the party's first commitments, made in opposition that year.

Labor won government in 2022 and legislated the state's Voice to Parliament in March 2023. It has held power since, winning a second term earlier this year.

The federal Voice to Parliament suffered a major setback in October 2023, when just over 60 per cent of Australians rejected a constitutional referendum to recognise Indigenous people and establish a national advisory body, with every state and territory except the ACT voting No.

South Australia though, had already legislated its own Voice to Parliament before the referendum. Maher rejected the argument the No result should halt the state's plans.

"This is about something we committed seven years ago to do in South Australia, and we will take that commitment," he told NITV on Sunday, referencing the 2019 pledge Labor made in opposition and carried into government.

"What was voted on at the referendum was to change the federal constitution, to firstly recognise Aboriginal people — recognise the oldest living culture this planet's ever seen — but also to establish an advisory body."

He acknowledged not everyone was behind him. "I wouldn't say there's no division," Maher said, adding that the issue still generates dozens of letters to his office each month.

The body — a 12-member State Voice drawn from six regional bodies, all elected by and from First Nations South Australians — advises parliament and government on health, education, justice and other matters affecting their communities.

Maher said the first part of the state's efforts was spent building the machinery of a body. Without a national precedent, he likened the work to "building the plane as you're flying it".

title.en: The ideas that Australia started — that the world followed
title.zh: 澳大利亚开创并被世界效仿的理念

summary.en: A report highlights Australia's significant contributions to global innovation, with ideas ranging from road safety measures to democratic practices being adopted worldwide.
summary.zh: 一份报告指出，澳大利亚对全球创新做出了重大贡献，其在道路安全措施和民主实践等方面的理念已被世界各地采纳。

body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the names and images of Indigenous persons who have passed away.

In December 2025, Australia became the first country to legislate a social media ban for children under the age of 16.

While the jury is still out on its effectiveness , the laws introduced world-first penalties for social media giants that are caught breaking the rules.

Now, a range of countries — including Britain, France and Malaysia — look set to follow suit, something that Australian policymakers have taken as a point of pride.

In late June, the prime minister's office put out a statement saying Australia had "started a global movement". Anthony Albanese himself said the nation was "leading the world".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's not the first time Australia has led the charge on ambitious legislation and inventions.

Lucie Shawcross — who has researched Australian ingenuity and inventiveness at the National Archives of Australia (NAA) — believes "there are just so many incredible [Australian] inventions out there that have made an impact globally".

"Spray-on skin is an Australian invention, the cochlear implant, WiFi," the exhibitions curator told SBS News. "There are some really profound inventions that have impacted upon all of us."

Other distinctly Australian inventions that have seen mass uptake include the dual flush toilet, Hills Hoist, the baby capsule, Aerogard and cask wine (also known as goon ), according to the NAA.

In 2012, Australia took the radical step of removing all branding from cigarette packaging, replacing it instead with plain packaging, public health warnings and confronting images of smoking-related illnesses.

The policy, introduced under Julia Gillard's Labor government, was designed to make smoking less "cool" — or, as Gillard herself wrote in The Guardian in 2013, "kill the glamour and substitute it with the facts: smoking equals death".

The move was widely opposed by cigarette companies who unsuccessfully sued the Australian government over the changes.

By 2016, plain packaging was included in guidelines to the World Health Organisation Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.

Now France, the UK, New Zealand, Norway, Ireland, Thailand, Uruguay, Saudi Arabia, Israel, Slovenia, Türkiye, Canada, Singapore, Belgium, the Netherlands and Georgia have all adopted similar policies.

Laws requiring motorists to use seatbelts are almost taken as natural now, but that wasn't always the case — Victoria became the first jurisdiction in the world to make seat belts compulsory in 1970.

body.en:

The approach to North Sullivan's home is a magical journey through winding eucalypt-lined roads, where traffic signs warn of wombats and roaming horses greet passing cars.

The driveway to the 71-year-old's home — aptly named Wombat Gully — is situated on the doorstep of Yengo National Park, part of the World Heritage-listed Greater Blue Mountains area, around two hours north-west of Sydney.

His property is one of 22 clustered in what they call Upper Yango, on the site of a former dairy farm that was subdivided into small hobby farms.

Sullivan says the landholders were a "very disparate community" prior to the Black Summer fires of 2019-20.

But friendships were formed as they fought side-by-side to protect their properties.

From the ashes of that traumatic experience emerged an enduring lesson: one of the most valuable assets in an emergency are the people around you.

The community is now one of many across Australia taking direct action to reduce the risks of fire and flood, as climate change is projected to increase the frequency and severity of such extreme weather events.

Since the fires, the Upper Yango community has developed wide tracks that double as firebreaks in strategic locations, as well as other measures to reduce fire risk to their properties.

However, Sullivan says these efforts are not reflected in their insurance premiums.

He is just one of many landowners SBS News has spoken to in NSW who are either struggling to find insurance cover or facing rising costs.

Some experts warn the pressures could leave some communities unviable, with implications that extend beyond remote and regional Australia.

As premiums continue to rise and access to cover becomes more challenging, communities are questioning whether efforts to reduce disaster risk will be enough to keep insurance affordable.

Professor Paula Jarzabkowski, an expert on insurance protection gaps at the University of Queensland, says there's already significant evidence that many Australians are struggling to get adequate cover for their properties — either because it's too expensive or because policies exclude specific risks, like certain types of flood or fire.

"Brisbane is built on a floodplain, parts of Sydney are built on floodplains, so we have seen catastrophic flooding in these major cities as well," she tells SBS News.
